title: {Syn} Benford Law Likes Leading Ones
content:
Benford law says that in many naturally occurring datasets, leading digit 1 appears much more often than leading digit 9. The probability for digit d is log10(1 + 1/d).

It works best for data spread across several orders of magnitude, which is why it appears in finance, populations, physical constants, and fraud screening.

Why it matters: math facts keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
